newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals mixed at PM gold fix.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals mixed at PM gold fix.

text.p: The platinum group metals were firmer on Thursday afternoon but gold was under pressure from a stronger dollar, dealers said.
The U.S. unit was off a six-year high against the mark and 43-month peak with the Swiss Franc but its strength was still enough to deter potential gold buyers.
At the afternoon fixing bullion was fixed at $321.95 per ounce, 15 cents above the morning setting but still $2.55 shy of the Wednesday close.
The Comex August futures contract was down $1.20 at $322.60, taking its lead from weaker markets in the Far East and Europe.
Overnight weakness came from fund and producer selling.
Some dealers in Europe reasoned that short covering and physical offtake would hold the downside at around $318.00.
But others noted stops lined up on Comex could trigger fresh 12-year lows if position holders hit the panic button.

News earlier that South Africa's Anglogold had already closed one shaft at its huge Freegold mining complex, had another ready to mothball and more marginal units would follow was only briefly helpful for the price.
Platinum and palladium turned firm after opening easier in Europe reflecting speculator profitaking on Tocom.
"There are still buyers around but sellers are very scarce," one dealer said adding that market activity in both metals in Europe had been very thin.
Deliveries following Russia's delayed start to its 1997 export campaign this month had been "sporadic" either to the contracted customers in Japan or to the European dealer market, the dealer said.
"Russian deals are not that common. Metal is just not flowing into Europe," he said.
One problem was that with Russia's exporters taking about two weeks to deliver to Zurich, dealers were mostly only willing to offer at a discount to the cash price.
"You have to borrow to finance the metal and at around 80 percent for a month that is expensive," a dealer said.
Even so dealers said physcial demand for palladium, especially, appeared to be holding up well depite high prices.
"It could be that industrial customers are opting to buy metal rather than lease it at these rates," a dealer said.
Palladium was indicated at $201.00/$204.00 up $4.60 and platinum was quoted at $417.50/$420.50, up $1.50.
Silver was quiet and a cent easier at $4.30/$4.32.
